html: אנת (the root of the pron. 2 pers. in Shemitic: أَنْتَ, አንተ anta; f. أَنْتِ, አንቲ: antī; Biblical Aramaic Kt אַנְתָּה (m.), 𝔗 אַנְתְּ & אַתְּ (both m. & f.); Syriac ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݀, f. ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݀ܝ, the n being written but not pronounced; Assyrian atta, f. atti-e Dl§ 55 a, the nt being merged in the double t; Heb. similarly. Pl. أَنْتُمْ, አንትሙ: f. أَنْتُنَّ, አንትn; Aramaic אַנְתּוּן, ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݀ܘܢ, f. אַתִּין, ܐܰܢ̱ܬܷ݀ܝܢ, Assyrian attunu).
